feedback.Physical Object: Excluded — A Boolean expression is abstract, not a tangible entity.
feedback.Synthetic: Included — It is a formal human-designed logical construct.
feedback.Biological/Biomimetic: Excluded — Not based on or inspired by biological systems.
feedback.Powered: Excluded — It is inert unless evaluated in a system.
feedback.Structural: Excluded — Has no physical architecture or embodiment.
feedback.Observable: Excluded — Only its representation (e.g., in code or text) is visible.
feedback.Physical Medium: Excluded — Exists independently of any particular medium.
feedback.Active: Excluded — It does not initiate processes or effects autonomously.
feedback.Intentionally Designed: Excluded — The expression is a symbolic structure, not a tool or mechanism.
feedback.Outputs Effect: Excluded — It encodes logic but does not produce output independently.
feedback.Processes Signals/Logic: Excluded — It is a structure to be processed, not a processor itself.
feedback.State-Transforming: Excluded — Used in logic but does not transform state inherently.
feedback.Human-Interactive: Excluded — Readable and writable, but not intrinsically interactive.
feedback.System-integrated: Excluded — Appears in systems, but is not embedded functionally.
feedback.Functionally Autonomous: Excluded — Cannot function or change without an interpreter or context.
feedback.System-Essential: Excluded — Not universally required; many systems use it, but it is not essential to all.
feedback.Symbolic: Included — Made of formal symbols and operators.
feedback.Signalling: Included — Conveys logical structure and conditions.
feedback.Rule-governed: Included — Syntax and semantics are strictly defined.
feedback.Compositional: Included — Built from simpler components using operators.
feedback.Normative: Included — Prescribes conditions for logical correctness and usage.
feedback.Meta: Included — Can express or manipulate logic itself (e.g., logical identities).
feedback.Temporal: Excluded — Static expression; does not evolve or act in time.
feedback.Digital/Virtual: Included — Exists purely in abstract/digital environments.
feedback.Social Construct: Included — Exists and functions through shared logical conventions.
feedback.Institutionally Defined: Included — Standardized in formal logic, computer science, and mathematics.
feedback.Identity-Linked: Excluded — Not tied to social or personal identity.
feedback.Regulated: Excluded — Not governed by policy or law.
feedback.Economically Significant: Excluded — Crucial in systems, but not economically transacted itself.
feedback.Politicised: Excluded — Not a site of political dispute.
feedback.Ritualised: Excluded — Not used in ceremonial or symbolic rituals.
feedback.Ethically Significant: Excluded — Logical operations are value-neutral; ethics arise in application.

encoding_notes: This encoding frames Boolean expressions as synthetic, symbolic, and compositional abstractions governed by strict logical norms. They are not functional artifacts themselves but are foundational to digital logic and formal reasoning. Their meaning arises from interpretation within systems, not intrinsic functionality.
